evidence.locator: Version 1.0; printed pp.15–17, Tables 3/4 (one-based PDF pp.19–21); printed pp.17–20, sections 4.4–4.5 and Tables 5/6 (PDF pp.21–24); printed p.14 waiver (PDF p.18)
evidence.claim: Demonstration 2: Vendor A met flight criteria but failed image quality; Vendor B had connectivity, waypoint and imagery limitations. Later Vendor A was disqualified; Vendor B met Templeton flight criteria but failed Silverado criteria. BVLOS permission and flight success did not establish accepted inspection output.

evidence.title: Drone blood delivery in Rwanda
evidence.publisher: Nisingizwe et al., Lancet Global Health
evidence.locator: Methods: Comparison of delivery times / Blood product expirations; Results: Table 1 shows / As hospitals use their vehicles; Tables 1–2; Discussion final two paragraphs and limitations; DOI 10.1016/S2214-109X(22)00048-1; April 2022 issue 10(4):e564–e569
evidence.claim: 20 facilities; 12,733 delivered orders, 5,517 emergency. Mean 49.6 min (95% CI 49.1–50.2) includes order preparation/packaging; median 41 min excludes it. Main estimated-road comparator is hospital-origin round trip; center-origin one-way sensitivity gives median advantages of 19 min (CBT estimates) and 28.5 min (Google Maps). The 67% expiration reduction is an interrupted-time-series estimate per facility at 12 months. Authors state drone delivery was more expensive than road delivery in Rwanda at publication; cost-effectiveness remains unresolved.
evidence.limitations: Nonrandomized and no control group; planned road-record collection was prevented by COVID-19 restrictions, so road counterfactual is estimated. Time comparison excludes drone preparation; all-in mean includes it. No cost amount, provider margin, causal health outcome or current performance established; accepted clinical-SLA fraction not reported.
evidence.access_history: Initial edition used PubMed abstract; revised after independent Exa retrieval of publisher full text on 2026-10-25. April 2022 is the journal issue date.
